title: HIS-201 Ch. 5 — 3 Numbers & Dates
subject: HIS-201
topic: Chapter 5: The Mosaic of Eighteenth-Century America

cards.term: When La Salle landed in Texas
cards.def: In 1684 La Salle's colonists, missing the Mississippi's mouth, landed on the Texas coast, where nearly 300 died and they killed La Salle.

cards.term: When Spain began Texas missions
cards.def: In 1690 Spain began establishing missions among Texas Indians as a buffer against the French.

cards.term: How Spain held Texas by the early 1720s
cards.def: By the early 1720s Spain held Texas with 10 Franciscan missions, 4 presidios and a small settlement on the San Antonio River.

cards.term: How many nonnatives lived in Texas in 1731
cards.def: In 1731 Texas had only about 500 nonnative settlers, and by 1760 that number had only slightly more than doubled.

cards.term: How deadly the Texas missions were
cards.def: In the 1730s smallpox killed over 1,000 mission Indians near San Antonio, and at Mission San Antonio only 1 in 3 newborns lived to age 3.

cards.term: When Spain reconquered New Mexico
cards.def: In 1692 Spanish colonists returned in earnest to New Mexico, from which Popé's Pueblo Revolt had driven them in 1680.

cards.term: When Villasur's expedition was destroyed
cards.def: On August 13, 1720, Pawnee warriors armed with French guns destroyed Villasur's expedition on the Platte River, killing Villasur and L'Archevêque.

cards.term: When the Comanches took over the Plains
cards.def: In the 1730s the Comanches, with European horses and guns, moved onto the Plains and eclipsed the Apaches.

cards.term: When Comanches and Spain made peace
cards.def: In 1786 Comanche leader Ecueracapa helped broker peace with Spain, opening a period of calm and growth in New Mexico.

cards.term: How many non-Indians lived in New Mexico by 1800
cards.def: By the end of the 1700s New Mexico's non-Indian population reached 20,000 after peace with the Comanches.

cards.term: When Spain first explored and then colonized California
cards.def: Spaniards first explored California's coast in 1542, but the Crown authorized permanent colonization only in 1768.

cards.term: When California's overland route closed
cards.def: After 1781 a Yuma Indian uprising closed the Colorado River crossing, so Spain abandoned the overland route to California.

cards.term: How large Spanish California was by 1800
cards.def: By 1800 Spanish California had four presidios, three towns, 18 Franciscan missions with 13,000 Indian converts, and only about 1,800 Hispanic residents.

cards.term: How many French lived along the St. Lawrence by 1760
cards.def: By 1760 about 75,000 French colonists, soldiers and priests lived in the St. Lawrence valley, mostly through natural increase.

cards.term: When the Le Pesant case occurred
cards.def: In 1706 Le Pesant's followers killed a priest and a French soldier near Fort Detroit, leading to the staged trial and escape.

cards.term: When Louisiana was founded
cards.def: In 1698 Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville founded French Louisiana with a post at Biloxi Bay.

cards.term: When New Orleans was founded
cards.def: In 1718 the French founded New Orleans, whose colonists soon demanded slaves for plantations.

cards.term: When the Company of the Indies brought slaves to Louisiana
cards.def: In 1719 the Company of the Indies brought nearly 6,000 slaves, overwhelmingly men, directly from Africa to Louisiana.

cards.term: When the Natchez rose against the French
cards.def: In 1729 the Natchez, joined by some newly arrived slaves, rose against the French and killed or captured about 500 colonists.

cards.term: How many French settlers Louisiana lost and kept
cards.def: By 1731 two-thirds of the French who came to Louisiana had died or fled, but nearly 4,000 French lived there by 1746.

cards.term: When King William's War was fought
cards.def: King William's War was fought from 1689 to 1697.

cards.term: When Queen Anne's War was fought
cards.def: Queen Anne's War was fought from 1702 to 1713, followed by about 25 years of Anglo-French "cold war."

cards.term: How many British and French colonists there were in 1720
cards.def: In 1720 Britain had nearly 400,000 colonial subjects and France only about 25,000, yet France's Indian alliances blocked British expansion west of the Appalachians.

cards.term: How many Scots-Irish, Germans and Africans came in the 1700s
cards.def: In the 1700s about 250,000 Africans in chains, about 250,000 Scots-Irish and about 135,000 Germans came to the British colonies.

cards.term: How high the colonial birthrate was
cards.def: The colonial birthrate was triple today's, with most women bearing five to eight children and most children surviving to adulthood.

cards.term: How fast China's and Europe's populations grew
cards.def: In the 1700s China grew from 150 million to over 313 million and Europe from about 118 million to 187 million.

cards.term: When Germans and Scots-Irish poured into western Pennsylvania
cards.def: By the 1720s Germans, Scots-Irish and native-born colonists were pouring into western Pennsylvania and the southern backcountry.

cards.term: How deadly the Atlantic crossing was for passengers
cards.def: Death rates on emigrant ships ran from 3 percent to as high as 10 to 15 percent, nearly comparable to slave ships.

cards.term: When New York's tenants rebelled
cards.def: New York's Hudson valley tenants rose in armed insurrection in 1757 and again, more violently, in 1766.

cards.term: How big colonial seaports were in 1750
cards.def: By 1750 the colonial seaports had only 8,000 to 22,000 people each, and seaport dwellers made up about 1 in 20 Americans.

cards.term: How many Africans arrived in northern seaports
cards.def: In the two decades after 1730 one-third of all arrivals in New York harbor were black, and by 1760 blacks were over three-quarters of Philadelphia's bound laborers.

cards.term: How many seaport women worked outside the home
cards.def: Fewer than 10 percent of seaport women worked outside their own homes.

cards.term: How many Americans were of African ancestry in 1775
cards.def: By 1775 one in five Americans was of African ancestry, and over 90 percent of black Americans lived in the South.

cards.term: When slave imports to the South peaked
cards.def: The four decades after 1700 were the heaviest years of slave importation to the Chesapeake and Carolina.

cards.term: How big Lower South and Chesapeake plantations were
cards.def: Lower South rice plantations held as many as 50 slaves, about half African-born, while Chesapeake plantations usually had fewer than 20.

cards.term: How outnumbered enslaved women were
cards.def: Among slaves, women were outnumbered two to one by men, so African-born women waited two or three years to marry and some men never found wives.

cards.term: How many Tidewater slaves were moved inland
cards.def: From 1755 to 1782 masters resettled one-third of all adult African Americans in Tidewater Virginia, breaking families apart.

cards.term: When the Stono Rebellion occurred
cards.def: In 1739 nearly 100 Africans led by Jemmy rose in South Carolina's Stono Rebellion, the largest slave revolt of the colonial period.

cards.term: When Harvard and Yale were founded
cards.def: Harvard was founded in 1636 and Yale in 1701, first to train ministers and later lawyers, merchants, doctors and scientists.

cards.term: How many colonists attended church
cards.def: About 80 percent of northern colonists attended church on the Sabbath, compared with about half in the South.

cards.term: When the Great Awakening began
cards.def: The Great Awakening first appeared in the 1730s among Presbyterians and Congregationalists in the middle colonies and New England.

cards.term: When Whitefield toured the colonies
cards.def: George Whitefield arrived in fall 1739 and preached from Georgia to New Hampshire for two years, sailing home in 1741.

cards.term: When Presbyterian and Baptist churches spread south
cards.def: From the mid-1740s to the 1770s scores of new Presbyterian and Baptist churches formed in the South and backcountry.

cards.term: How much colonial consumption of British goods rose
cards.def: Per capita colonial consumption of imported British manufactures rose 120 percent between 1750 and 1773.

cards.term: How many colonists lived in small towns
cards.def: In 1750 London had 675,000 people, while 90 percent of colonists lived in towns of under 2,000.

cards.term: How unequal English landownership was
cards.def: Just 2 percent of England's population owned 70 percent of the land.

cards.term: How big the middle class was in England and America
cards.def: Less than one-third of the English were middle class, compared with nearly three-quarters of white colonists.

cards.term: How much higher American wages were
cards.def: Wages in America were 100 percent higher than in England, making it easier to save and buy a farm.

cards.term: How many could vote in England and the colonies
cards.def: About a quarter of English adult men could vote, while over half of white adult colonial men could.

cards.term: How many MPs held Crown offices
cards.def: By the mid-1700s almost half of England's members of Parliament held Crown offices or government contracts.

cards.term: When the war that changed the empire began
cards.def: In 1754 a new war began in the American borderlands, one in which Indians proved decisive.
